We have committed an initial $750,000 to incubate and launch a third-party trust infrastructure for managed access to bio-capable AI models. We hope this project can make legitimate access easy for the scientists who need these tools, and hard for anyone who would misuse them. A shared credentialing system lets a researcher prove their credentials once and carry that verification across the platforms and providers they work with, instead of repeating the same checks for every model. Over time, such a system can leverage network effects by working across providers to improve decisions and intercept misuse. The project is led by Jonas Sandbrink and Nick de Raad, working as Entrepreneurs-in-Residence at Sentinel Bio. We provided Epoch AI with a $15,000 grant to expand their database of biological AI models with additional data annotations. Specifically, Epoch will add input and output type classifications to each of the 1,150+ models in their existing database – capturing both broad categories (such as amino acid sequences or molecular graphs) and precise data formats where available. This work builds on Epoch’s prior database releases supported by Sentinel Bio. We expect these enhanced annotations to improve the usability of the database for policymakers and researchers seeking to understand the technical landscape of biological AI tools.

In August 2025, Sentinel Bio provided $132,000 to the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovation (CEPI) to promote the responsible development of and reduce biosecurity risks associated with CEPI’s Pandemic Preparedness Engine. The Pandemic Preparedness Engine is a global artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled vaccine design platform to support the 100 Days Mission, an initiative to develop vaccines against novel viral threats with epidemic or pandemic potential within 100 days of identification. The grant will enable CEPI to retain an AI/biosecurity expert who will design and implement biosecurity safeguards for the Engine, including managed access approaches that will help ensure safe, secure, and equitable access to this global capability. The AI/biosecurity expert will also support CEPI’s broader biosecurity policy development across its diverse vaccine research, development, and manufacturing portfolio, totaling $3.8B across 47 countries to date. We anticipate that the AI/biosecurity framework and mitigations developed through this partnership will support global norm and best practices development and serve as a model for other AI developers and networks that, like CEPI, are working to integrate biosecurity best practices as core components of their funding, research, results communication, and partnerships.

We provided $600,000 to support a large-scale randomized controlled study examining whether frontier AI systems enable non-experts to perform expert-level biological tasks. This comprehensive wet lab study compares novice participants using AI assistance against a control group with internet-only access while completing multi-step laboratory procedures. The experiment aims to assess AI uplift capabilities in biological research, informing misuse risk assessments and model-level safeguards. Given the potential sensitivity of our findings, results will undergo pre-review by an independent advisory board of biosafety and national security experts before publication. We co-funded this effort with the Frontier Model Forum, an industry-supported non-profit organization dedicated to ensuring the safe and responsible development of frontier AI systems.

The project partner will create a risk assessment framework that categorizes varying biological types by risk level and evaluates under which specific circumstances they might meaningfully advance concerning capabilities. We expect this work to close critical knowledge gaps about how AI-based tools contribute to biosecurity risks. The project aims to produce clear, accessible guides for policymakers and inform more targeted mitigation strategies.

We expect this research project will help measure progress on implementing biosecurity safeguards for AI-Bio models, enabling evidence-based tracking of improvements in both the prevalence and quality of crucial safety measures.
